sections.title: Choose the first workflow
paragraphs: For a first sales webinar, keep the campaign limited to registration, a usable attendee room, a clear offer and a suitable follow-up path. For a repeat demo, decide whether instant on-demand or a scheduled automated session suits the audience.

For customer onboarding, use webinar education language and do not promise learning paths or certificates. For a client programme, resolve brand separation and permissions before duplicating the campaign across accounts.

This page explains the requirement in the context of EasyWebinar and preserves the supplied inventory status. Read the evidence section before treating an explanation of buyer value as a promise of current product support.

sections.title: Prepare the smallest useful event
paragraphs: Choose one topic, one audience and one next action. Pick live, automated or on-demand delivery based on the actual availability and staffing needs. Select an eligible plan and confirm the required attendee capacity.

Prepare the presentation, registration copy, speaker assets and offer destination. If the guided AI builder drafts these assets, review them for factual accuracy and unsupported claims before event configuration.

sections.title: Rehearse the entire attendee journey
paragraphs: Use a test registration in the intended browser and device. Verify confirmation, reminder and join information. Run the presentation, audience interaction and offer path, and inspect the recording, reports and follow-up.

If a CRM, checkout or external stream is involved, test the receiving system as well. A working room does not prove a completed purchase, successful sync or external stream permission. Resolve failures before sending the public invitation.

sections.title: Review and reuse
paragraphs: Inspect registration, attendance, watch time and supported conversion data using documented definitions. Use questions and drop-off points to improve the presentation rather than automatically interpreting every metric as buyer intent.

If the live presentation is approved for reuse, evaluate the live-to-evergreen workflow and confirm which assets and settings carry over. Test recorded playback and timed interactions before launching an automated campaign.

pages.title: Pricing, eligibility and plan scope
pages.publication: Verify policy, service or evidence before publishing
pages.description: Pricing, eligibility and plan scope: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.
intro: A webinar plan should be evaluated against the required delivery format, simultaneous attendees, integrations, usage and exit terms. The cheapest live plan is not automatically the cheapest plan that supports automation.

This review draft uses the supplied 16 September 2026 plan matrix as a dated reference. It does not provide a current purchase quotation or imply that those prices and limits remain unchanged. Resolve the production pricing and structured-data contradictions before release.

sections.title: Plan matrix — source dated 16 September 2026
paragraphs: Launch: monthly reference $44; annual-equivalent monthly reference $36; live / automated allocation 50 / 0. Source notes: Live only; AI builder 2 funnels/month; presenter-count wording needs confirmation.

Growth: monthly reference $116; annual-equivalent monthly reference $96; live / automated allocation 200 / 1,000. Source notes: Automation, simulive/evergreen, EasyCRM, checkout, EasyCast; listed CRM/email integrations.
Pro: monthly reference $198; annual-equivalent monthly reference $165; live / automated allocation 500 / 2,500. Source notes: Lead scoring; API scope requires confirmation.

Scale: monthly reference $349; annual-equivalent monthly reference $291; live / automated allocation 1,000 / 5,000. Source notes: Routing; full API; webhooks; SSO/SAML; white-label scope requires confirmation.

Enterprise: monthly reference Contact sales; annual-equivalent monthly reference Contact sales; live / automated allocation Disputed maximum. Source notes: Custom quotation; do not publish a confirmed 100,000-attendee guarantee.

sections.title: How to compare total cost
paragraphs: Count the lowest eligible plan, external CRM and email subscriptions you retain, processor charges, SMS or sending usage, any overages and implementation effort. A tool already owned is not automatically a saving just because a similar module exists in the webinar platform.

For an automated funnel, use the lowest plan that actually enables automation. For a one-off live session, compare the event’s genuine requirements before choosing a broader stack. Current purchase terms and cancellation rights need validation.

answers.question: What is this feature or requirement for?
paragraphs: Simulated chat replays configured chat activity alongside a recorded webinar session.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It can add context to the recorded presentation and show questions that were discussed during its original delivery.

answers.question: What happens if you do not have it?
paragraphs: A replay may lack the accompanying conversation, leaving references to chat or audience reactions unclear.

answers.question: Why should it matter to the buyer?
paragraphs: It matters when contextual chat is useful; replayed or simulated messages should not imply that those viewers are currently present.

paragraphs: The organiser can evaluate reuse of relevant audience questions around the recorded presentation.

answers.question: What happens if you do not have it?

paragraphs: Use a current product demo and a test contact in the existing CRM. Follow registration, viewing, CTA interaction and the resulting handoff.

The requirements below are the complete 25-item buyer set from the supplied inventory. They describe what this audience looks for, including needs that are unconfirmed or unavailable. Do not read an aspirational requirement title as a guaranteed business result.

sections.title: A practical workflow for this buyer
paragraphs: Prepare two sample client events with different brands. Verify separation of assets and records, the required permissions and the cost of the intended account arrangement.

intro: This workflow is for small businesses and solo operators evaluating a first sales webinar or a small repeat programme. The aim is a manageable next step toward an offer, using supported webinar delivery, attendee interaction and the appropriate next-action path.

The requirements below are the complete 25-item buyer set from the supplied inventory. They describe what this audience looks for, including needs that are unconfirmed or unavailable. Do not read an aspirational requirement title as a guaranteed business result.

sections.title: A practical workflow for this buyer
paragraphs: Start with one offer, one event and one follow-up route. Skip optional modules until the simplest useful attendee journey works and its cost is understood.

Begin with mandatory constraints: the event format, intended audience, required next action, existing stack and budget. Validate those before adding optional AI, CRM or multistream modules. Use the linked shared capability pages to inspect the actual product evidence.

pages.description: Enterprise teams with webinar programs: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.
intro: This workflow is for enterprise evaluators evaluating a governed webinar programme with mandatory procurement requirements. The aim is an approved operational and procurement decision, using supported webinar delivery, attendee interaction and the appropriate next-action path.

The requirements below are the complete 22-item buyer set from the supplied inventory. They describe what this audience looks for, including needs that are unconfirmed or unavailable. Do not read an aspirational requirement title as a guaranteed business result.

sections.title: A practical workflow for this buyer
paragraphs: Separate mandatory controls from desirable features. Request written evidence for each required capacity, security, access and service commitment before running a high-stakes programme.

Begin with mandatory constraints: the event format, intended audience, required next action, existing stack and budget. Validate those before adding optional AI, CRM or multistream modules. Use the linked shared capability pages to inspect the actual product evidence.

intro: This workflow is for B2B marketing teams evaluating a repeat webinar programme for demand generation and sales handoff. The aim is a documented lead or pipeline handoff, using supported webinar delivery, attendee interaction and the appropriate next-action path.

The requirements below are the complete 45-item buyer set from the supplied inventory. They describe what this audience looks for, including needs that are unconfirmed or unavailable. Do not read an aspirational requirement title as a guaranteed business result.

sections.title: A practical workflow for this buyer
paragraphs: Run a sample marketing webinar with a known test contact. Check the room experience, campaign source, engagement record and the actual receiving CRM object.

Begin with mandatory constraints: the event format, intended audience, required next action, existing stack and budget. Validate those before adding optional AI, CRM or multistream modules. Use the linked shared capability pages to inspect the actual product evidence.

pages.publication: Internal editorial review
intro: EasyWebinar is a webinar platform for businesses using live, automated and on-demand presentations to sell offers, generate leads and educate customers. This knowledge base explains the product modules, supporting microfeatures, buying constraints and evidence requirements in the supplied parameter inventory.

The core workflow is to develop a presentation, test it with a live audience and reuse an approved version through evergreen or on-demand delivery. Registration, audience interaction, offers, attendee data and relevant follow-up are documented as parts of that workflow rather than isolated marketing labels.

This is a version 1 editorial draft for team feedback. Supported, partial, unconfirmed and unavailable labels reflect the supplied source. They are not a fresh product audit. Unconfirmed capabilities are explained as requirements, while known gaps remain visible as limitations.

sections.title: Where to start
paragraphs: Choose the delivery job first: a live event, a repeatable recorded presentation, or immediate on-demand access. Then inspect the supporting features required to register, engage and follow up with the intended audience.

Already own a CRM? Keep it in the evaluation and inspect the actual integration. Already have a converting presentation? Focus on delivery and follow-up rather than assuming AI script generation is required. Need the simplest workflow? Begin with one event and only its necessary modules.

pages.description: Source method and reading the inventory: detailed EasyWebinar documentation covering purpose, benefits, tradeoffs, availability and review evidence.
pages.publication: Internal editorial review
intro: The primary source is the attached “Webinar Platform — The Complete Buyer & AI Evaluation Parameter Inventory.” It records 571 parameters: 186 universal, 48 commercial/trust/service/risk, 272 across ten buyer sets, and 65 AI-algorithm signals. All 571 IDs are preserved.

The source says Have and Claimed draw on EasyWebinar pages read on 30 September 2026, the 16 September 2026 plan matrix and earlier positioning inventories. AI recognition comes from a comparison diagnostic captured on 21–22 September 2026. The status snapshot is historical evidence; the draft date is not a new verification date.

sections.title: How to interpret the source columns
paragraphs: Have records whether the source identifies support: yes, partial or plan-gated, no, or unconfirmed. Claimed records whether the public website states the fact. AI records whether the diagnostic credited the product with it. Those three columns are separate and are preserved alongside each explanation.

Weight records how much the requirement affects the particular buyer’s decision: high, medium or low. A high weight does not change an unknown into a supported feature. AI editorial requirements have no product-availability status and are labelled accordingly.

sections.title: The buyer’s gates, in order
paragraphs: The source orders the buyer’s checks as job fit, attendee experience, existing-stack fit, price at the intended scale, ease of setup, proof from a relevant customer and operational or exit risk. Documentation should answer that sequence instead of listing every feature as equally important.

The draft’s solution hubs follow concrete jobs: course selling, coaching, product demos, demand generation, launches, onboarding, client campaigns, first webinars, governed teams and vertical seminars. Each relevant buyer requirement has a detailed section and a link to the underlying capability.

sections.title: The AI evidence gates
paragraphs: The source describes category fit, constraint satisfaction, corroboration, recency, lack of contradiction and buyer-branch coverage. This draft responds with direct feature explanations, traceable statuses and shared canonical capability pages.

A new document can improve what the vendor explains; it cannot by itself create independent reviews, fix external profiles or guarantee recommendation. The 65 AI requirements are therefore treated as an implementation and evidence checklist.

sections.title: Purchase jobs and product boundaries
paragraphs: The strongest proposed jobs in the source are selling through webinars and scaling a presentation through live-to-evergreen delivery. Pipeline generation is also relevant, while onboarding and launches require checking their particular requirements.

Internal meetings, accredited learning programmes, multi-track conferences and self-hosted or open-source delivery are outside the recommended product scope in the source. Buyers with those mandatory requirements should evaluate a suitable product category.

sections.title: How source recommendations were handled
paragraphs: The source includes suggested follow-up tasks, profile updates, a named colleague and a thirty-day re-run. Those are document recommendations, not instructions from you to message people, update review platforms or schedule work. This implementation uses them as context and retains the unresolved evidence tasks.

sections.title: Obsidian and current Google Doc review
paragraphs: The EasyWebinar-specific vault folder contained 870 Markdown files. All were scanned and indexed for this task; relevant product references, feature-rollout notes, help map and recent call notes were read in detail. Competitor captures and raw diagnostic answers are context, not EasyWebinar capability proof. Unrelated client folders were excluded.

The linked master Google Doc was read alongside the attached inventory, including its strategy, positioning, site architecture and parameter tabs. Recommendations inside those files remain source context rather than new instructions to edit third-party profiles or contact colleagues.

The additional 52 controls retain dated provenance. The March rollout supports native MP4 hosting and distinct paid-registration and room-offer journeys; its attendee analytics release is explicitly Beta. The May update names 11 live-room languages. September notes add EasyCRM modules and attendee-overage clarification. Roadmap email reporting, global in-room language switching, native SMS, WhatsApp and agentic moderation still require shipping evidence.

sections.title: Product and workflow context
paragraphs: Native MP4 video hosting sits in the live production layer of the webinar workflow. Evaluate it together with the event format, the account’s eligible plan and any external provider involved. Its detailed parameter explanation below covers both the benefit and the limits of relying on it.

The supplied source is an inventory rather than a current implementation manual. Exact configuration steps, UI screenshots and supported limits must be attached during review; this draft does not invent button labels or silently substitute a different feature.

intro: Flodesk through Zapier is documented here as a unconfirmed connection. The purpose is to connect the relevant webinar workflow with a system the business already uses; it is not a promise of complete two-way sync or every feature offered by that provider.

Evaluate this connection using a real event and a test record or transaction. Availability, authentication, eligible plan, transferred events and receiving data must be confirmed for Flodesk through Zapier specifically rather than copied from another integration.

sections.title: What this connection is for
paragraphs: For Flodesk through Zapier, start by naming the exact job: transferring a registration, recording an attendance event, sending a follow-up, receiving a purchase event or linking to a next action. Choose only the job supported by the actual connection. This makes the setup testable and prevents a logo from standing in for an integration specification.

The connection can reduce repeated manual entry and preserve continuity with the existing stack when the required action is supported. Without it, the team needs a verified middleware, API, export or manual route; those alternatives have their own operating cost and failure modes.

sections.title: Scope the team must verify
paragraphs: Confirm the current Flodesk through Zapier connector or workflow, authentication method, account permissions, eligible plan, trigger and action list, receiving objects, transferred fields, event timing and supported direction. For a payment tool, also confirm the checkout path and what purchase, cancellation or refund information actually returns.

Test a new record, an existing record and a deliberate failure. Document deduplication, retries, unsupported fields, required external subscriptions and the way the operator can inspect an error. Do not imply certified-partner status or a field count without direct evidence.
